patterns.comment: A body whose %LANGUAGE line states LD or FBD — the ONE place networks are read (openspec language-line: the stated language decides how a body is read, never its content). ST may hold `NETWORK := TRUE;` (a variable named NETWORK), so sniffing a NETWORK line would paint the rest of an ST file as network text; an UNSUPPORTED body holds nothing. The line itself is coloured with the main grammar`s language-line names, since this injection wins the line. Ends, by lookahead, at the closing keyword of the unit that owns the body, which the main grammar then colours.
patterns.name: meta.body.network.vg

patterns.comment: A network-text network — the textual form of an FBD/LD body (volt-cli docs/network-text.html). Read only inside a body stated LD or FBD (meta.body.network.vg). The header carries no order number and no language; its optional fields are NAMED and come in one order — LABEL: the jump target, DISABLED the vendor's bit, TITLE: free text with IEC's $-escapes — and it ends at its newline. `\b` after NETWORK keeps a variable such as NETWORK_OK an identifier. Mirrors the LSP's network-text parser header.
patterns.name: meta.network.vg

patterns.comment: Backticked text is ONE operand, target or call head whose text is not a single token (`fc_dinttotime(T.Start,2)`, `arr[i + 1]`) — verbatim between the backticks (a backtick doubled, IEC's $ escapes), never parsed into boxes. Matched before the ST grammar so its parentheses and operators are not coloured as structure.
patterns.name: variable.other.quoted.vg

patterns.comment: A split point (B6): `split<VarId>`, the vendor Demux, defined by `split1 := value;` and read by name. The pattern is reserved (P1) — a variable of that shape is backticked — so the name alone tells a split.
patterns.name: variable.other.wire.vg

patterns.comment: ENO and EN follow a box's outputs, ENO where the box shows it and EN last (`MOVE 1 => x ENO EN c`); BRANCH opens a parallel's branch list and SHORTCIRCUIT states its mode. Words of the text: a variable spelled like one is backticked.
patterns.name: keyword.other.eno.vg

patterns.comment: A box is its NAME (B1, B2): ADD SUB MUL DIV GT GE EQ NE LE LT and MOVE, infix or in the call form (AND OR XOR MOD are the ST grammar's operators already).
patterns.name: keyword.operator.word.vg

patterns.comment: The edge flags R_EDGE x / F_EDGE x, prefixes on their operand (not an R_TRIG box), never part of a longer name or between backticks.
patterns.name: keyword.other.construct.vg
